title: Parking penalties system and asset management funding
subtitle: Scheifele Bridge replacement, record transit ridership, and a delegation on petitions and public consultation.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended that the Region adopt administrative monetary penalties for parking tickets on Regional roads {{vote:m3}}. Instead of going to Provincial Offences Court, disputes would go to a screening officer who can keep, reduce or cancel a fine. Staff said this lowers court costs and generally raises revenue, and that Cambridge, Kitchener and Waterloo asked for it. The committee also asked staff to report back on how fines are reviewed, who is involved and what the current system is.

The committee also recommended approving the design concept for the Scheifele Bridge replacement on Northfield Drive at the Conestogo River in Woolwich. Staff would file the Notice of Completion and place the Environmental Study Report on the public record for 30 days.

Staff presented on asset management and capital budget alignment, and the report was received for information. Under other business, staff reported record ridership on September 7 of about 134,000 GRT riders and 20,000 LRT riders. Staff said they are reviewing the delays and may propose operational changes in next year's budget. The committee asked for regular updates on transit, including good news. A delegate spoke on public consultation and petitions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended amending the Traffic and Parking By-law so administrative penalties can be used for parking on Regional roads, as set out in Schedule A {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended approving the project design concept for the Scheifele Bridge replacement on Northfield Drive at the Conestogo River, and directed staff to file the Notice of Completion and place the Environmental Study Report on the public record for 30 days.

debate: On parking penalties, one councillor questioned how fine amounts are set, noting that parking on LRT tracks seemed more dangerous than some other infractions yet carried a lower fine. Another said a blocked LRT line can disrupt the whole system.

Staff said the new system does not change the set fines. Screening officers can only keep or reduce a fine, and the system is audited. Staff added that officers rarely reduce accessible-parking fines.

Councillors preferred asking staff for a report on how fines are reviewed rather than directing changes themselves. One councillor said a review of fines is already under way in several municipalities.

On asset management, staff said reserve contributions are meant to keep reserves sustainable over the long term so the Region can avoid borrowing for renewal work. Councillors asked which reserves are legally required and how the two funding shortfalls differ. Staff said the water reserve is required by legislation, and few others are.

On transit, councillors asked about the causes of delays, notifications to riders and crowding on the LRT. Staff said crowding lengthens boarding times, and that more frequent trains would come before longer ones.
